title: Runes
subtitle: Artifacts from the Gates that each supply one magical Word
summary: A Rune is an artifact recovered from a Gate that supplies one magical Word. It goes inert after use, and nobody knows how to make one.
content:
> *"A Rune is a sentence in a language we did not know we were reading."*
> — chalked on a laboratory blackboard in Endros

A **Rune** is an artifact recovered from inside a [[gates|Gate]] that supplies one magical [[words|Word]]. Runes aren't a human technology. They came out of the Gates already working.

Before anyone cast a spell, researchers found that certain markings, gestures and positions could make an impossible effect happen when a suitable Rune was nearby, and happen again the next time. That was **runework**: careful, empirical and almost without theory. Only later did it turn out that each Rune was supplying one Word.

A Rune makes its Word **available**: someone who knows a [[forms|Form]] that needs that Word can use the Rune's Word instead of producing it themselves. With a `Move` Rune at hand, anyone who knows Kinetic Shove can cast it.

After use, a Rune goes **inert**. It doesn't crumble or vanish; it just stops showing any sign of being active. Whether it's spent, discharged, single-use or degrading is one of the field's favourite arguments. (A Vard's view: *"If my lathe stopped and looked like this, I wouldn't say it was spent. I'd say it was off."*)

Nobody knows how to make one. Every Rune in use came from a Gate, and whether people could ever manufacture them is the question every power in [[endros|Endros]] is watching. The rules for using one: [Runes](game.html#post-runes).
